Hypothesis: We hypothesize that a dual precision gene therapy strategy, implemented specifically in hepatocytes using advanced viral vectors and CRISPR-based transcriptional activation systems integrated with real-time molecular imaging, can concurrently enhance mitoNEET (CISD1) activity and upregulate the system Xc⁻ antiporter. By augmenting mitoNEET function, the therapy will reduce the labile iron pool, thereby mitigating the Fenton reaction—a primary source of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Simultaneously, boosting system Xc⁻ expression will enhance cystine uptake and glutathione synthesis, which in turn stabilizes GPX4 and prevents its degradation due to ROS-mediated lipid peroxidation. This dual intervention is expected to break the cascade of events leading to ferroptosis—from iron overload to mitochondrial damage—thereby reducing hepatocyte death and attenuating liver injury. Integrated monitoring strategies will further ensure therapeutic specificity and safety by tracking changes in mitochondrial iron levels, ROS production, and gene activation in real time.
Abstract: This study proposes a hepatocyte-targeted dual precision gene therapy that leverages advanced CRISPR-based transcriptional activation and next-generation viral vector systems to restore mitochondrial iron homeostasis and bolster antioxidant defenses. Specifically, our approach aims to enhance mitoNEET (CISD1) function to lower the labile iron pool—thereby attenuating the Fenton reaction—and concurrently upregulate system Xc⁻ to drive glutathione synthesis and preserve GPX4 functionality. Integrated real-time molecular imaging and safety monitoring tools will be employed to track mitochondrial iron levels, ROS dynamics, and gene activation specificity, ensuring efficacy while minimizing off-target effects. By directly addressing the key steps in the iron overload-induced ferroptotic cascade, this strategy is poised to reduce mitochondrial lipid peroxidation, prevent ferroptotic cell death, and ultimately ameliorate liver injury.
CausalChain: Iron overload in liver -> Excess labile iron fuels Fenton reaction -> Elevated ROS production increases mitochondrial lipid peroxidation -> Impaired mitoNEET function exacerbates mitochondrial iron dysregulation -> Amplified lipid peroxidation compromises GPX4 (and system Xc⁻ activity) triggering ferroptosis -> Hepatocyte death intensifies liver injury -> Enhanced mitoNEET function plus upregulated system Xc⁻/GPX4 axis (via precision gene therapy and advanced monitoring) restores iron-homeostasis, reduces ROS and lipid peroxidation, and prevents ferroptosis
